findings.summary: Falsy string check on `body` (and `html` at line 159) treats empty string `""` as not-provided, raising ValueError for a valid empty-body email
findings.failure_scenario: A workflow YAML passes `body: ""` (empty body, e.g. subject-only notification). The `elif body:` check treats `""` as falsy, falls through to the `else` branch, and raises `ValueError("Either 'body' or 'html' must be provided")` -- crashing the workflow even though a body was explicitly supplied. Fix: use `if html is not None` / `elif body is not None`.

findings.summary: User-controlled SMTP settings (`settings.host`, `settings.port`) interpolated into HTML test email body via `.format()` without any HTML escaping
findings.failure_scenario: An admin sets the SMTP host to `smtp.example.com"><script>alert(1)</script>` or any string containing angle brackets. The `.format()` call embeds this raw value into the HTML email body, producing malformed or injected markup in the test email delivered to the admin's inbox.

findings.summary: Falsy check on `body` and `html` in `_notify` return dict omits keys when value is empty string, causing inconsistent return shape
findings.failure_scenario: A workflow sends an HTML-only email (no `body`). `_notify` returns `{"from": ..., "to": ..., "subject": ...}` without a `body` key. If a downstream workflow action or template references `{{ steps.send.results.body }}`, it gets nothing (or an error if the engine strictly dereferences missing keys) -- whereas callers that previously always received a `body` key (from the old code that unconditionally included it) are now broken when HTML is used instead of plain text.
